title: Avoid With locoregional Analgesia Persistant Postoperative Pain After Surgery In Children
official: Avoid With locoregional Analgesia Persistant Postoperative Pain After Surgery In Children
summary: Main objective: To show the positive impact of locoregional Analgesia in the prevention of persistant postoperative Pain after orthopedic trauma surgery in children

interventions.name: PARACETAMOL B BRAUN 10 mg/ml, solution pour perfusion
NALBUPHINE RENAUDIN 20 mg/2 ml, solution injectable
SUXAMETHONIUM AGUETTANT 10 mg/mL, solution injectable en seringue préremplie
SUFENTANIL VIATRIS 5 microgrammes/ml, solution injectable (IV ou péridurale)
DOLIPRANE 150 mg, poudre pour solution buvable en sachet-dose
PROPOFOL LIPURO 1 % (10 mg/ml), émulsion injectable ou pour perfusion
DEXAMETHASONE VIATRIS 4 mg/1 ml, solution injectable en ampoule
SEVOFLURANE BAXTER 1 ml/ml, liquide pour inhalation par vapeur
INTRALIPIDE 20 POUR CENT, émulsion pour perfusion.
KETOPROFENE MEDISOL 100 mg/4 ml, solution à diluer pour perfusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 5 years and < 15 years and 3 month
2. Indication for surgical treatment of a fracture by osteosynthesis
3. Patient affiliated to the social security system
4. Informed and signed consent of patient and one of the two holders of parental authority
5. Conscious patient (Glasgow score =15)
6. Patient can give a verbal assessment of their pain
Exclusion criteria:
1. Refusal to participate by one of the two holders of parental authority or by the child
2. atrioventricular conduction disorders
3. Sensory neurological deficit of the operated limb on preoperative examination
4. Ischemia of the operated limb on preoperative examination
5. Polytrauma patient
6. Known allergy to Mepivacaine
7. Patient included in a category 1 interventional clinical trial of analgesic therapy
8. Patient on anticoagulant drugs
9. Epilepsy not controlled by a treatment
10. Porphyria
